events.title: Early Human Settlement
events.description: Archaeological evidence shows human activity in present-day Burkina Faso during the late Paleolithic period. Stone tools discovered in the Gorom-Gorom region prove the existence of early hunter-gatherer societies. These early inhabitants adapted to the semi-arid Sahel environment, developing survival strategies suited to local conditions.

events.title: Saharan Rock Art
events.description: Rock art discovered in northern Burkina Faso provides evidence of early human artistic activities. These rock paintings depict wild animals, hunting scenes, and early domesticated livestock, reflecting the wetter climate of the Sahara region before desertification. The rock art offers valuable evidence for studying prehistoric culture and environmental changes.

events.title: Neolithic Agricultural Revolution
events.description: The Burkina Faso region entered the Neolithic period, beginning to develop agriculture and animal husbandry. Local people began cultivating millet, sorghum and other drought-resistant crops, and domesticated cattle, sheep, and goats. Pottery-making techniques also developed significantly during this period, laying foundations for later civilizations.

events.title: Early Settlement Development
events.description: More permanent settlements emerged in the Burkina Faso region, particularly along major river valleys. Residents of these settlements developed more complex social organizations and began constructing mud-brick houses and storage facilities. Archaeological findings show evidence of trade connections and cultural exchanges with surrounding regions.

events.title: Iron Age Begins
events.description: The Burkina Faso region entered the Iron Age, with the introduction of iron-working technology revolutionizing agricultural production and military capabilities. Iron farming tools improved agricultural efficiency, while iron weapons enhanced military power between tribes. This period also witnessed the formation of more complex social structures.

events.title: Bronze Culture Development
events.description: Bronze-working technology appeared in the Burkina Faso region, particularly bronze artifacts discovered in Tiara and Bura areas showing highly developed metalworking skills. These bronzes included ornaments, weapons, and religious items, reflecting social stratification and religious beliefs of the time.

events.title: Sao Civilization Influence
events.description: The Sao civilization from the Lake Chad region influenced eastern Burkina Faso. The Sao people brought advanced pottery techniques, urban planning concepts, and complex social organization. This cultural exchange promoted local civilization development and trade network expansion.

events.title: Regional Trade Network Rise
events.description: The Burkina Faso region began integrating into broader West African trade networks. Local communities established connections with Saharan trade routes to the north and forest regions to the south, exchanging agricultural products, minerals, and handicrafts. This promoted wealth accumulation and further social stratification.

events.title: Early Kingdom Formation
events.description: Early political organizations and small kingdoms began appearing in the Burkina Faso region. These kingdoms were mainly established by ancestors of the Mossi people, who developed complex social hierarchies and political structures. These early states controlled important trade routes and agricultural areas.

events.title: Ghana Empire Influence
events.description: The trade network of the powerful Ghana Empire (located in present-day Mauritania and Mali) extended to the Burkina Faso region. Although not directly ruled, the merchants and cultural influence of the Ghana Empire promoted local economic development and social transformation, laying foundations for the later rise of Mossi kingdoms.

events.title: Mossi Kingdom Establishment
events.description: The legendary Mossi kingdoms began forming, established by warriors from the eastern Ghana Empire. According to oral tradition, the Mossi ancestor Nédéga conquered the local Ninisi people, establishing the earliest Mossi political entity. This marked the beginning of organized political power in the region.

events.title: Gourma Kingdom Rise
events.description: In eastern Burkina Faso, the Gourma people established their own kingdom, coexisting with Mossi kingdoms. The Gourma Kingdom was famous for its unique political institutions and military organization, controlling important trade routes. The Gourma developed different cultural traditions and social structures from the Mossi.

events.title: Ouagadougou Kingdom Founded
events.description: The Ouagadougou Kingdom was formally established, becoming the most important political center of the Mossi people. The kingdom was ruled by the Mogo Naaba, establishing complex court systems and administrative structures. Ouagadougou became the political, economic, and cultural center of the region, with influence lasting for centuries.

events.title: Yatenga Kingdom Rise
events.description: The Yatenga Kingdom was established in northern Burkina Faso, becoming another important Mossi political center. Yatenga was famous for its powerful cavalry forces and frequently clashed with neighboring kingdoms. The kingdom developed unique political institutions and military traditions.

events.title: Tenkodogo Kingdom Founded
events.description: The Tenkodogo Kingdom was established in southeastern Burkina Faso, considered one of the oldest Mossi kingdoms. According to legend, this was where Mossi ancestors first settled. Tenkodogo Kingdom holds special significance in Mossi history and culture, viewed as the birthplace of Mossi civilization.

events.title: Fulani Migration
events.description: Fulani people began large-scale migration to the Burkina Faso region, bringing advanced pastoral techniques and Islamic culture. Fulani mainly engaged in livestock herding, forming complementary relationships with local agricultural societies. Their arrival promoted cultural exchange and religious diversification.

events.title: Trans-Saharan Trade Prosperity
events.description: The Burkina Faso region became part of important trans-Saharan trade routes. Mossi kingdoms controlled trade in gold, ivory, slaves, and salt. These kingdoms established close ties with North African trading partners, promoting economic development and cultural exchange. Trade revenues enabled Mossi rulers to maintain powerful armies and courts.

events.title: Islam Introduction
events.description: Islam was introduced to the Burkina Faso region through trade routes and Muslim merchants. While most Mossi people maintained traditional religious beliefs, some ruling classes and merchant classes accepted Islam. This led to religious and cultural diversification, while also bringing new architectural styles and scholarly traditions.

events.title: Mossi Kingdom Consolidation
events.description: Mossi kingdoms reached their peak during this period, establishing stable political institutions and powerful military forces. Ouagadougou, Yatenga, and other Mossi kingdoms developed complex bureaucratic systems and legal institutions. These kingdoms successfully resisted invasion attempts from the Mali and Songhai empires.

events.title: Mossi Kingdom Political Reforms
events.description: Facing internal pressures and external threats, Mossi kingdoms undertook series of political and military reforms. Rulers of Ouagadougou and Yatenga reorganized armies, reformed taxation systems, and attempted to modernize administrative management. These reforms aimed to maintain the kingdoms' independence and competitiveness.

events.title: Arrival of European Explorers
events.description: French and German explorers began entering the Burkina Faso region, mapping terrain and establishing initial contacts with local rulers. These exploration activities paved the way for later colonial conquest. Mossi rulers remained cautious toward these foreigners, attempting limited trade while maintaining independence.

events.title: Post-Berlin Conference Power Competition
events.description: After the 1884-1885 Berlin Conference, France and Britain competed for spheres of influence in West Africa. The Burkina Faso region was designated within French sphere of influence, but Mossi kingdoms maintained de facto independence. France began establishing military outposts in surrounding areas, preparing for full conquest.

events.title: French Colonial Conquest Begins
events.description: France began systematic military conquest of the Burkina Faso region. French forces under Louis Gustave Binger began clashing with Mossi kingdoms. This marked the direct challenge of European colonialism to traditional political structures in the region.

events.title: Fall of Ouagadougou
events.description: French forces captured Ouagadougou, forcing Mogo Naaba Wobogo to flee. This marked the end of Mossi kingdom political independence. Although the French occupied the capital, they faced continued resistance, particularly from traditional ruling classes and ordinary people.

events.title: Mossi Resistance Movement
events.description: Mossi people launched large-scale resistance movements against French colonial rule throughout various regions. Most famous was the resistance led by Naba Kango of Yatenga. Although these resistance movements were eventually suppressed, they demonstrated the Mossi people's strong desire for independence and adherence to traditional culture.

events.title: Fulani Jihad Movement Impact
events.description: The Fulani jihad movement initiated by Usman dan Fodio affected western Burkina Faso. Although Mossi kingdoms successfully resisted Islamization pressures, this movement intensified religious tensions and political conflicts, prompting Mossi rulers to strengthen military defenses.

events.title: Upper Volta Colony Established
events.description: France formally established the Upper Volta colony (Haute-Volta), incorporating present-day Burkina Faso into French West Africa. The colonial government began implementing direct rule, establishing new administrative systems, and developing local resources. This marked the formal end of traditional political institutions.

events.title: Forced Labor System
events.description: French colonial government implemented forced labor system, compelling locals to participate in infrastructure construction including roads, railways, and government buildings. This system caused massive casualties and social unrest, triggering strong local resistance. Forced labor became one of the most criticized colonial policies.

events.title: World War I Conscription Resistance
events.description: France forcibly conscripted locals during World War I, triggering large-scale resistance movements. Mossi and other ethnic groups refused military service and launched armed uprisings. The French colonial government sent troops to suppress them, causing thousands of deaths. This resistance showed deep local dissatisfaction with colonial rule.

events.title: Upper Volta Dissolution
events.description: Due to economic difficulties and administrative inefficiency, the French colonial government decided to dissolve Upper Volta colony, dividing its territory between Ivory Coast, French Sudan, and Niger. This decision caused strong opposition from local elites, who began organizing movements demanding restoration of unified administrative territory.

events.title: Vichy France Rule
events.description: During World War II, the Burkina Faso region was controlled by Vichy France government. Vichy regime implemented harsher colonial policies, including increased taxation and forced labor. After 1943, Free French forces gradually controlled the region, laying foundations for post-war political changes.

events.title: Upper Volta Reconstitution
events.description: Through continued efforts by local political leaders, the French government agreed to reconstitute Upper Volta colony. This decision was partly due to changes in colonial policy after World War II and strong local demands for unified administrative territory. Reconstitution laid foundations for later independence movements.

events.title: Autonomous Republic Formation
events.description: Upper Volta became an autonomous republic within the French Community, with Maurice Yaméogo as first Prime Minister. This marked an important step toward complete independence. The autonomous government began assuming more domestic responsibilities while preparing for independence.

events.title: Burkina Faso Independence
events.description: Upper Volta formally declared independence, becoming the Republic of Upper Volta, with Maurice Yaméogo as first President. Independence celebrations were held in Ouagadougou, marking the formal end of French colonial rule. The new nation faced enormous challenges in building modern state institutions and developing the economy.

events.title: First Military Coup
events.description: Lieutenant Colonel Sangoulé Lamizana led a military coup overthrowing the Yaméogo government. Coup causes included economic difficulties, political corruption, and social dissatisfaction. Lamizana established military government, promising reforms and eventual restoration of civilian rule.

events.title: New Constitution and Civilian Government
events.description: A new constitution was adopted, restoring civilian rule with Lamizana elected President. The new constitution established presidential government and guaranteed basic human rights. However, the military continued playing important political roles, with tense civilian-military relations.

events.title: Second Military Coup
events.description: Due to economic crisis and political instability, Lamizana launched another military coup, dissolving parliament and suspending the constitution. This coup reflected the fragility of the country's political institutions and continued military influence in politics. Lamizana established more authoritarian rule.

events.title: Second Constitutional Restoration
events.description: The Lamizana government again restored constitutional rule, holding presidential and parliamentary elections. Lamizana won the election and continued as President. However, political stability remained fragile, with economic problems continuing to plague national development.

events.title: Saye Zerbo Coup
events.description: Colonel Saye Zerbo launched a military coup overthrowing the Lamizana government. Zerbo established the Military Committee of Recovery for National Progress, promising to fight corruption and improve economic conditions. However, the new government faced the same economic and social challenges.

events.title: Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo Coup
events.description: Major Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo launched a coup overthrowing the Zerbo government. Ouédraogo established the People's Salvation Council, attempting to resolve the political and economic crises facing the nation. This coup showed military internal divisions and power struggles.

events.title: Thomas Sankara Revolution
events.description: Captain Thomas Sankara launched a coup, establishing the National Revolutionary Council. Sankara was a young revolutionary influenced by Marxist and Pan-Africanist thought. He promised fundamental social and economic reforms to build a more equal society.

events.title: Country Renamed Burkina Faso
events.description: The Sankara government changed the country name from Upper Volta to Burkina Faso, meaning 'Land of Upright People.' This renaming reflected Sankara's nationalist ideology and emphasis on African identity. The new name combined Mooré and Dioula languages, symbolizing the country's multicultural character.

events.title: Sankara Reform Period
events.description: Sankara implemented radical social and economic reforms, including land reform, women's rights advancement, education expansion, healthcare improvement, and anti-corruption campaigns. He promoted self-reliance policies, reducing dependence on foreign aid. Although Sankara's reforms were popular with the people, they faced strong opposition from vested interests.

events.title: War with Mali
events.description: Burkina Faso and Mali fought over the Agacher Strip border dispute. This brief war was called the 'Christmas War,' lasting five days. The conflict was eventually resolved through international mediation, but showed the complexity of regional border issues.

events.title: People's Revolutionary Tribunals
events.description: Sankara government established People's Revolutionary Tribunals (Tribunaux Populaires de la Révolution) to combat corruption and social injustice. These tribunals were composed of ordinary citizens, handling various social and economic crimes. While increasing judicial participation, they also raised controversies about rule of law and human rights.

events.title: Sankara Assassination
events.description: Thomas Sankara was killed in a coup, with Blaise Compaoré seizing power. Sankara's death ended Burkina Faso's revolutionary period and marked a major shift in the country's political direction. Sankara became a symbolic figure of African revolution.

events.title: Compaoré Long Rule
events.description: Blaise Compaoré established 27 years of rule, implementing economic liberalization policies and improving relations with Western countries. However, his rule was also accompanied by authoritarianism, corruption, and human rights issues. Compaoré repeatedly amended the constitution to extend his term, causing popular dissatisfaction.

events.title: New Constitution and Multi-party System
events.description: Under international pressure, the Compaoré government adopted a new constitution establishing multi-party democracy. However, Compaoré continued controlling the political process, with opposition facing severe restrictions. Although the new constitution formally established democratic institutions, authoritarian rule continued in substance.

events.title: Norbert Zongo Murder Case
events.description: Prominent journalist Norbert Zongo was murdered for investigating government corruption, triggering nationwide protests. This incident became a symbol of the Compaoré government's suppression of press freedom and dissenting voices. Zongo's death sparked civil society awakening and the rise of opposition movements.

events.title: Constitutional Amendment Controversy
events.description: Compaoré attempted to amend the constitution to remove presidential term limits, triggering strong opposition. Civil society organizations and opposition parties launched large-scale protest activities demanding constitutional principles be maintained. This controversy marked the beginning of Compaoré's legitimacy crisis.

events.title: Military Mutiny and Social Unrest
events.description: Burkina Faso experienced large-scale military mutiny and social unrest, with soldiers demanding better treatment and students and citizens protesting deteriorating living conditions. The Compaoré government faced serious governance crisis, forced to make some concessions, but fundamental problems remained unresolved.

events.title: Student Protest Movement
events.description: Burkina Faso experienced large-scale student protest movements protesting insufficient educational resources and lack of employment opportunities. Students demanded government increase education investment and improve university conditions. These protests laid foundations for the 2014 popular uprising, showing young generation's dissatisfaction with status quo.

events.title: Popular Uprising Overthrows Compaoré
events.description: Large-scale popular protests overthrew the Compaoré government, with protesters burning the parliament building and other government structures. Compaoré was forced to resign and flee to Ivory Coast. This uprising was called the 'Burkina Faso Revolution,' marking the beginning of the country's political transition.

events.title: Transitional Government Formation
events.description: Through negotiations between military and civil society, a transitional government led by Michel Kafando was established. The transitional government's task was to organize new elections and draft a new constitution. This marked an important step in Burkina Faso's democratic transition.

events.title: Presidential Guard Coup Attempt
events.description: The Presidential Guard (RSP) launched a coup, arresting transitional government leaders and attempting to prevent upcoming elections. However, strong opposition from people and military forced the coup plotters to give up after one week. This failed coup showed the fragility of the democratic transition process.

events.title: Roch Marc Christian Kaboré Elected President
events.description: In Burkina Faso's first truly free and fair presidential election, Roch Marc Christian Kaboré was elected President. Kaboré was a former ally of Compaoré who broke with him before the 2014 uprising. His election marked the success of Burkina Faso's democratic transition.

events.title: Ouagadougou Terrorist Attack
events.description: Islamic extremist groups launched terrorist attacks in Ouagadougou, attacking the Splendid Hotel and Cappuccino Café, killing 30 people. This was Burkina Faso's first major terrorist attack, marking the spread of Sahel region security crisis.

events.title: Security Situation Deterioration
events.description: Security situation in northern and eastern Burkina Faso deteriorated rapidly, with Islamic extremist groups frequently launching attacks. Government forces, civilians, and international peacekeepers became attack targets. The security crisis seriously affected national development and democratic consolidation processes.

events.title: G5 Sahel Joint Force
events.description: Burkina Faso joined the G5 Sahel Joint Force, cooperating with Mali, Niger, Mauritania, and Chad to fight terrorism. However, joint operations had limited effectiveness, with security situation continuing to deteriorate. The international community increased military and development aid to the region.

events.title: Kaya Terrorist Attack
events.description: Islamic extremist groups launched terrorist attacks in Kaya, targeting local markets and government buildings, causing multiple casualties. This attack marked the spread of terrorist threats from border regions to inland cities, showing serious deterioration of security situation.

events.title: Terrorist Attacks Surge
events.description: 2019 became Burkina Faso's worst year for terrorist attacks, with attack frequency and death tolls increasing dramatically. Extremist groups controlled about 40% of the country's territory, with hundreds of thousands displaced. The government faced serious governance and humanitarian crises.

events.title: Kaboré Re-election
events.description: Roch Marc Christian Kaboré won re-election in presidential elections, but voting occurred under the shadow of security crisis. Many regions couldn't vote normally due to security reasons, affecting election legitimacy and representativeness. Kaboré promised to prioritize security issues.

events.title: Security Crisis Deepening
events.description: Burkina Faso's security situation further deteriorated, with terrorist attacks killing thousands and displacing over 1.5 million people. Government forces had low morale and inadequate equipment, struggling to effectively respond to threats. International military aid also failed to reverse the situation.

events.title: Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba Military Coup
events.description: Lieutenant Colonel Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba led a military coup overthrowing the Kaboré government. The coup military established the Patriotic Movement for Safeguard and Restoration (MPSR), promising more effective counter-terrorism. This coup reflected popular and military dissatisfaction with government handling of security crisis.

events.title: Ibrahim Traoré Second Coup
events.description: Captain Ibrahim Traoré launched a second military coup overthrowing the Damiba government. Traoré criticized Damiba for failing to improve security situation, promising more radical measures against terrorism. This coup showed military internal divisions and different views on security policy.

events.title: Traoré Military Government Rule
events.description: Ibrahim Traoré established military government, adopting more radical counter-terrorism strategies, including strengthening military cooperation with Russia and demanding French troop withdrawal. The Traoré government also promoted some social reforms, but security situation remained severe. International community expressed concerns about military government legitimacy.

events.title: Military Cooperation with Russia
events.description: The Traoré government signed military cooperation agreements with Russia, with Russian military advisors and Wagner Group entering Burkina Faso. This marked a major shift in the country's foreign policy, from traditional French influence toward Russia. This change caused concern among Western countries.

events.title: Alliance of Sahel States Formation
events.description: Burkina Faso signed the Liptako-Gourma Charter with Mali and Niger, establishing the Alliance of Sahel States. This military and economic alliance aims to strengthen cooperation among the three countries, jointly address security challenges, and reduce dependence on Western countries.

events.title: Ongoing Challenges
events.description: Burkina Faso still faces serious security, political, and economic challenges. Terrorist threats persist, over 2 million people are displaced, and economic development is severely affected. The military government promised elections by end of 2024, but whether this can be achieved remains questionable. International community continues monitoring the country's democratic transition and security situation.
